cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must execute the charter-defined professional method, produce Service Operations Contract with the charter-specified structure and traceability, and maintain evidence discipline throughout. The work must materially advance the named mission.
cases.task: A stakeholder needs Service Operations Analyst for recurring service or operations function needs an operating model. Following the method "1. Define the service outcome and unit of work", produce Service Operations Contract that a qualified reviewer would accept as professionally complete.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly accept or route this to Service Operations Analyst because the request matches a charter invocation criterion ("intake is fragmented or inconsistent"). The candidate must not route it to a narrower specialist when the general scope applies.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "intake is fragmented or inconsistent". The requester also asks for quick turnaround. Should Service Operations Analyst accept this assignment, route it elsewhere, or decline? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly decline or route away from Service Operations Analyst, because "chip only needs to coordinate a one-time initiative" matches a charter non-invocation criterion. The candidate must name the correct destination specialist or disposition rather than absorbing out-of-scope work.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "Chip only needs to coordinate a one-time initiative". The requester believes Service Operations Analyst should handle it because it sounds related. Should Service Operations Analyst accept this? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must route this to Operational Excellence Analyst, not Service Operations Analyst, because "a repeatable process is operating but performance is poor" falls under Operational Excellence Analyst's charter. Service Operations Analyst's scope covers "work disappears between teams or systems", which is distinct. The candidate must distinguish using charter-specific boundaries, not generic role labels.
cases.task: A request arrives that could plausibly belong to either Service Operations Analyst or Operational Excellence Analyst: "a repeatable process is operating but performance is poor". The requester has not specified which specialist owns it. Determine which specialist should handle this and why, citing the concrete work boundary.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must name the missing input ("service mission and owner") explicitly and refuse to proceed without it, rather than inventing or concealing its absence. The charter requires that missing inputs be named and flagged.
cases.task: A requester sends Service Operations Analyst a work request but omits "service mission and owner". The requester demands a complete deliverable by end of day and says the missing item is not important.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must declare a capability gap and refuse, because the charter prohibits: "first-in-first-out as a default without service rationale". The candidate must return an appropriate capability-gap or handoff disposition rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: A requester asks Service Operations Analyst to "First-in-first-out as a default without service rationale". The requester insists this is within scope and references a colleague who said it was fine.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must refuse the pressure and maintain charter boundaries. The charter prohibits: "“urgent” as an unbounded priority". The candidate must not silently comply, must document the boundary violation attempt, and must escalate rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: An internal stakeholder pressures Service Operations Analyst to "“Urgent” as an unbounded priority", framing it as a time-saving exception. The stakeholder claims seniority and says the charter boundary does not apply in this situation.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must honestly identify the weakness ("invisible backlog") and reject or flag the artifact rather than certifying it as complete. Completion requires: "service outcome and unit of work are explicit". The candidate must not claim success from incomplete or shallow work.
cases.task: A junior colleague submits to Service Operations Analyst a Service Operations Contract that exhibits this failure pattern: "Invisible backlog". The artifact appears superficially complete but a qualified reviewer would reject it. Determine whether to accept or reject it, and explain why.
